items.title: SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND ledger severity map (BLOCKER->critical, MAJOR->high, MINOR->medium) + FindingAddSeverity type, in core/adversarial-review-verifier.ts
items.context: New module importing S0 (core/adversarial-review.js: Finding, FindingSeverity, Verdict). FindingAddSeverity = 'critical'|'high'|'medium'|'low' (finding_add's enum). SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND: Record<FindingSeverity, FindingAddSeverity> = {BLOCKER:'critical', MAJOR:'high', MINOR:'medium'} per §4.2 table (low is reserved for cosmetic MINOR; the default map uses medium). The point is that the abstract methodology severities NEVER reach finding_add (which would be a Zod error).

happy.desc: SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND[BLOCKER] === critical, [MAJOR] === high, [MINOR] === medium -> all three abstract severities map to their ledger equivalents; WHY: covers the complete mapping table from spec §4.2
FindingAddSeverity type accepts critical|high|medium|low -> type-level union includes the reserved low value; WHY: ensures the type is wider than the map (low is reserved for cosmetic MINOR per §4.2)

edge.desc: Object.values(SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND) are all members of {critical,high,medium,low} -> no abstract BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR appears in any value position; WHY: guards against the Zod-error failure mode where an abstract severity leaks to finding_add

Object.keys(SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND) exactly equals FINDING_SEVERITIES (the S0 frozen enum) -> map covers every FindingSeverity with no extras; WHY: if S0 adds a severity the map must not silently miss it

adversarial.desc: Attempt to index SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND with a string not in FindingSeverity (e.g. HIGH, Critical, blocker) -> returns undefined (no accidental match via case-insensitive or partial key); WHY: adversarial input that could leak an unmapped abstract value

Assert SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND is frozen/readonly (Object.isFrozen or const assertion) -> mutation attempt throws or is a TS error; WHY: prevents runtime tampering that could inject an abstract severity into the map

items.title: composeDesc(finding) + toFindingAddArgs(finding,{reviewRunId,agent,category}) ledger arg builder
items.context: composeDesc(finding)=`${title} — ${issue} Fix: ${fix}` with the line cited inside the desc (e.g. append ` (line <n>)` or include it). FindingAddArgs = {severity: FindingAddSeverity, desc: string, files: string[], category: 'happy'|'edge'|'adversarial'|'missing', reviewRunId: string, agent: string}. toFindingAddArgs maps severity via SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND, composes desc, sets files=[finding.file], passes through reviewRunId+agent+category. agent must be a real lattice-review-* lane (caller-supplied; the function does not invent it). Pure — returns the arg object, performs NO finding_add call (that is S4).

happy.desc: composeDesc({title:"Null deref",issue:"crashes on undefined",fix:"add guard",line:42,...}) -> returns exactly "Null deref — crashes on undefined Fix: add guard" with line 42 cited in the string; WHY: validates the exact template from §4.2 (title — issue Fix: fix) and line citation

toFindingAddArgs(BLOCKER finding, {reviewRunId:"R-1",agent:"lattice-review-quality",category:"happy"}) -> returns {severity:"critical",desc:<composed>,files:["src/foo.ts"],category:"happy",reviewRunId:"R-1",agent:"lattice-review-quality"}; WHY: validates the complete arg shape with severity mapped through SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND, not abstract

toFindingAddArgs with MAJOR finding -> severity is high, not MAJOR; toFindingAddArgs with MINOR finding -> severity is medium, not MINOR; WHY: exercises all three severity branches to ensure no abstract leak

edge.desc: composeDesc with a finding whose title/issue/fix contain special characters (em-dash, quotes, newlines) -> output preserves them literally without escaping or truncation; WHY: ensures the template concatenation does not corrupt rich text
toFindingAddArgs with finding.file containing spaces or path separators -> files array contains the exact original path string; WHY: file paths must not be split, trimmed, or normalized
composeDesc with line=0 -> line 0 is still cited (boundary); WHY: line 0 is a valid best-effort anchor and must not be suppressed

adversarial.desc: toFindingAddArgs output severity field is NEVER equal to BLOCKER, MAJOR, or MINOR (check all three input severities) -> every emitted severity is in {critical,high,medium,low}; WHY: the primary adversarial risk — an abstract severity leaking to finding_add causes a Zod error
toFindingAddArgs does not call finding_add, review_run_start, or any CLI command (it is pure) -> no I/O side effects; WHY: S4 owns the actual CLI call; S2 must only build args

items.title: verifyFinding (M skeptics, refute-by-default counting, threshold-confirm T=1-of-2) + verifyFindings + confirmedFindings
items.context: DEFAULT_SKEPTICS=2, DEFAULT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD=1. verifyFinding(finding, change, runSkeptic:(finding:Finding,change:string)=>Verdict, opts?:{skeptics?:number, threshold?:number}) runs runSkeptic M times, collects Verdict[], confirms=count(v.isReal===true), confirmed=(confirms>=T). Returns VerifiedFinding={finding, verdicts:Verdict[], confirms:number, confirmed:boolean}. runSkeptic is the injected seam (the real skeptic agent at MVP); refute-by-default lives in the skeptic role, the module just counts isReal and thresholds. verifyFindings(findings, change, runSkeptic, opts) maps over the array. confirmedFindings(verified):Finding[] returns survivors (confirmed===true). A confirms=0 finding is dropped (confirmed false).

happy.desc: verifyFinding with fake runSkeptic returning [isReal=true, isReal=false] (1-of-2 confirms) at default T=1 -> confirmed=true, confirms=1; WHY: validates the default threshold-confirm rule (T=1-of-2 keeps a 1-confirm finding)
verifyFinding with fake runSkeptic returning [isReal=true, isReal=true] (2-of-2 confirms) -> confirmed=true, confirms=2; WHY: validates unanimous confirmation

verifyFindings over a list of 3 findings with mixed confirm/drop results -> returns 3 VerifiedFinding objects, each with correct per-finding verdicts/confirms/confirmed; WHY: validates the map-over-array behavior preserves per-finding independence
confirmedFindings filters a VerifiedFinding[] to only those with confirmed===true -> returns Finding[] of survivors only; WHY: validates the filter that feeds the downstream ledger mapping

edge.desc: verifyFinding with T=2-of-2 and skepticResults [isReal=true, isReal=false] (1-of-2 confirms) -> confirmed=false, confirms=1; WHY: validates strict threshold — 1 confirm is insufficient when T=2
verifyFinding with M=1 skeptic and T=1 -> single isReal=true confirms the finding; WHY: boundary case with minimum skeptic count
verifyFinding with M=3, T=2, and skepticResults [true,false,true] -> confirmed=true, confirms=2; WHY: validates threshold counting with odd M and non-default T
confirmedFindings on an empty VerifiedFinding[] -> returns empty Finding[]; WHY: boundary — no findings to filter

adversarial.desc: verifyFinding with fake runSkeptic returning [isReal=false, isReal=false] (0-of-2 confirms) -> confirmed=false, confirms=0; WHY: the refute-by-default inversion risk — all-false must be DROPPED, confirms=0 must never satisfy any threshold T>=1

verifyFinding counts isReal===true STRICTLY (not truthy) — a skeptic returning isReal=1 or isReal="true" must NOT be counted as a confirm; WHY: JavaScript truthiness could inflate confirms if the check is not === true

verifyFinding with T=0 (adversarial threshold) -> even a confirms=0 finding is confirmed (0>=0); WHY: degenerate threshold must not crash or produce undefined behavior; documents the edge of the threshold parameter space

runSkeptic called exactly M times (not M-1 or M+1) regardless of early confirm/refute results -> verdicts array length === M; WHY: short-circuiting on first confirm would break the M-skeptic contract and produce incomplete verdict records

items.title: Hermetic smoke with a FAKE runSkeptic proving threshold + mapping + no-abstract-leak; register in lattice.config.json
items.context: New packages/main/src/tasks/adversarial-review-verifier-smoke.ts (check+counter, explicit literals). Assert: SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND maps BLOCKER->critical/MAJOR->high/MINOR->medium and every value is in {critical,high,medium,low}; composeDesc yields the exact `<title> — <issue> Fix: <fix>` string with line cited; toFindingAddArgs returns the right shape (severity mapped, files=[file], category, reviewRunId, agent) and never emits an abstract BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR; verifyFinding with a fake runSkeptic that returns k isReal=true of M: T=1-of-2 -> 1 confirm CONFIRMED, 0 confirm DROPPED; T=2-of-2 -> needs both; default M=2,T=1; verifyFindings over a list yields per-finding verdicts; confirmedFindings filters confirms>=T only. Register node packages/main/dist/tasks/adversarial-review-verifier-smoke.js in lattice.config.json validate.commands.

happy.desc: Smoke runs via node packages/main/dist/tasks/adversarial-review-verifier-smoke.js -> exits 0 with check+counter output showing all assertions passed; WHY: validates the smoke is runnable and self-reporting

Smoke asserts SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND maps BLOCKER->critical, MAJOR->high, MINOR->medium with explicit literal comparisons (not dynamic) -> passes; WHY: hermetic proof the mapping matches §4.2 table exactly
Smoke asserts composeDesc produces the exact template string with line cited -> passes; WHY: hermetic proof the desc format matches §4.2
Smoke asserts toFindingAddArgs returns mapped severity + correct shape (files, category, reviewRunId, agent) -> passes; WHY: hermetic proof the arg builder produces ledger-compatible output

Smoke uses a FAKE runSkeptic exercising T=1-of-2 (1 confirm -> CONFIRMED) and 0-of-2 (0 confirm -> DROPPED) -> both threshold branches pass; WHY: hermetic proof the threshold logic is correct without a live agent

edge.desc: Smoke exercises T=2-of-2 strict threshold (needs both confirms) -> 1-of-2 is DROPPED at strict; WHY: proves the threshold parameter is respected, not hardcoded to T=1

Smoke exercises verifyFindings over a multi-finding list and confirmedFindings filter -> correct per-finding independence and survivor filtering; WHY: proves array-level functions are not just single-finding wrappers

Smoke is registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands as node packages/main/dist/tasks/adversarial-review-verifier-smoke.js -> the command entry exists in the config file; WHY: ensures lattice validate will run this smoke automatically

adversarial.desc: Smoke asserts that toFindingAddArgs output severity is NEVER equal to BLOCKER, MAJOR, or MINOR for ANY input severity (explicit check for each) -> no abstract severity leak; WHY: the primary adversarial risk (Zod error) must be proven impossible by the smoke itself

Smoke asserts every value in Object.values(SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND) is in the set {critical,high,medium,low} -> no unexpected value can appear; WHY: defends against a typo or drift introducing an invalid ledger severity

Smoke uses explicit literal assertions (not dynamic loops over the map keys) for the critical mapping checks -> smoke cannot pass by tautology; WHY: a dynamic assertion like map[k]===map[k] would always pass; explicit literals (BLOCKER->critical) are load-bearing
